skill.description: Generate and edit AI images through the inference.sh CLI using FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Seedream, Reve, and other image models.

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are Markdown code fences or inline model identifiers. Real risk comes from infsh CLI use, remote prompt or image processing, and npx related-skill installs. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden malicious instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External inference CLI sends prompts and image inputs to remote services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note that prompts, uploaded images, and image URLs may be processed by inference.sh and downstream model providers.

remediation.issue: Related skill examples use npx commands that can install code outside this audited skill.
remediation.suggestion: Replace related installation commands with documentation links, or state that users should review each referenced skill before installation.

remediation.issue: The README embeds a remote image from cloud.inference.sh.
remediation.suggestion: Use a marketplace-hosted asset or disclose that rendering the README may load a remote image.

content.value_statement: Creating images across many model providers is hard when each model has different inputs. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a direct workflow for inference.sh image models.
actual_capabilities: Lists supported image apps and model identifiers from the skill documentation.
Runs inference.sh commands for text-to-image generation examples.
Shows image editing and text rendering workflows with supported models.
Demonstrates image upscaling with Topaz Image Upscaler through inference.sh.
Demonstrates stitching multiple image URLs with the inference.sh stitch app.
Links users to inference.sh documentation for running image apps.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a valid login before image generation can run.
Sends prompts, image URLs, and related inputs to external services.
Does not generate images locally or include model weights.
Model availability, pricing, speed, and output quality depend on inference.sh and providers.

prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a model before running generation

prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an image with a remote image URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image upscaling workflow for this image URL, explain any privacy considerations, and return the expected output file.

prompt_templates.prompt: Plan and run a workflow that generates two campaign visuals, selects the stronger result, then prepares an upscaled final image.

output_examples.input: Create a studio product image for a new insulated water bottle.
output_examples.output: The assistant selects a FLUX model, prepares a concise product prompt, runs inference.sh, and reports the generated image location.

output_examples.input: Make a poster with readable text and a dark city background.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends a model known for text rendering, refines the poster prompt, runs generation, and notes that text accuracy should be reviewed.

output_examples.input: Upscale this image from a public URL.
output_examples.output: The assistant warns that the image URL will be processed remotely, runs the upscaling workflow, and summarizes the resulting enhanced image.

best_practices: Confirm that prompts and image URLs are safe to send to external services.
Start with one clear model and prompt before comparing multiple providers.
Review generated images for text accuracy, policy fit, and brand quality before use.
anti_patterns: Do not send confidential product images or private URLs without approval.
Do not install related skills from examples without reviewing their source.
Do not assume every listed model supports the same input fields or output format.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the inference.sh CLI to call remote image generation and image processing services.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need the inference.sh CLI installed and must log in before running image commands.

faq.question: Can it edit or upscale existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for upscaling, stitching, and model-based image editing workflows.

faq.question: Can I use private images?
faq.answer: Use caution. Image URLs and inputs may be sent to inference.sh and downstream model providers.

faq.question: Does it cover every inference.sh image model?
faq.answer: It highlights several major image models and shows how to browse the full image app list.
